tools.name: convert_subtitle
tools.description: Convert subtitle text between formats. Reads SRT, WebVTT, ASS/SSA, YouTube SBV and TTML/DFXP; writes SRT, WebVTT, ASS, CSV or plain text. Format is auto-detected unless `from` is given.

to.description: Target format. `text` = plain transcript, one line per cue, no timecodes.

dedupe.description: Only for to="text": collapse consecutive identical lines (rolling-caption transcripts repeat lines). Default false.

tools.name: clean_subtitles
tools.description: Strip noise from auto-generated subtitles: HTML/WebVTT tags, ASS override codes, music and sound-effect cues, speaker labels, empty cues and duplicate lines. Returns the subtitle file in SRT or WebVTT.

remove_tags.description: Strip HTML/WebVTT tags and ASS override codes. Default true.

remove_speaker_labels.description: Strip leading "SPEAKER:" prefixes. Default false — enable only if you want them gone.

drop_empty.description: Drop cues that become empty after cleaning. Default true.

drop_duplicates.description: Drop cues whose text was already seen. Default false.

to.description: Output format. Default: same as the input.

tools.name: retime_subtitles
tools.description: Fix subtitle timing. Use offset_seconds for a uniform shift (whole track early/late). Use ratio, or from_fps/to_fps, for progressive drift caused by a frame-rate mismatch. Pass exactly one of the three.

offset_seconds.description: Shift every cue by this many seconds. Negative = earlier. e.g. -2.5

ratio.description: Scale all timings by this factor (new = old x ratio). e.g. 1.0427 for a 25→23.976 fps fix.

from_fps.description: The frame rate the subtitles were authored for (used with to_fps).

to_fps.description: The frame rate of the actual video (used with from_fps).

tools.name: check_subtitle_timing
tools.description: Audit subtitle readability and produce a report: reading speed (CPS), cue durations that are too short or too long, lines that are too wide, more than two lines, and overlapping cues. Returns a formatted report listing every flagged cue.

min_duration_seconds.description: Minimum cue duration in seconds. Default 0.833 (Netflix 5/6s).

max_duration_seconds.description: Maximum cue duration in seconds. Default 7.

tools.name: merge_subtitles
tools.description: Append one subtitle track after another (CD1 + CD2, or a second language track). The second track is offset so it starts after the last cue of the first, plus an optional gap.

append_content.description: The subtitle file text to append.

gap_seconds.description: Extra gap between the two tracks, in seconds. Default 0.

to.description: Output format. Default: same as the input.

tools.name: split_subtitles
tools.description: Split one subtitle track into two parts at a given timecode, keeping original timecodes. Use the `at` argument plus `part` to fetch either half.

part.description: Which half to return. Default "a" (before the split point).

to.description: Output format. Default: same as the input.

tools.name: fix_subtitle_encoding
tools.description: Repair mojibake — text where UTF-8 bytes were decoded as a single-byte encoding (cp1252/Latin-1 or cp1251). Symptoms: "Ã©", "â€™", "Ð¿Ñ€Ð¸Ð²ÐµÑ‚". Returns the repaired text and how many passes were applied.

read_as.description: Which encoding the file was wrongly read as. Default "auto" (tries cp1252 then cp1251).

twice.description: Set true when the text was mis-decoded twice (nested mojibake). Default false.

tools.name: text_to_subtitles
tools.description: Turn a plain transcript (one line per caption) into an SRT file with evenly spaced timecodes. Timing is a starting point, not a real transcription — say so when you present the result.

content.description: Plain text, one caption per line. Blank lines are skipped.

duration_seconds.description: Seconds each cue stays on screen. Default 2.5.

start_seconds.description: Timecode of the first cue, in seconds. Default 0.

max_chars_per_cue.description: Split longer lines into several cues at word boundaries. Default 0 = never split.
